case_number: Civil Appeal No. 2665 of 2022 (Arising from SLP(C) No. 6062/2022 @ D.No. 18112/2017)
summary: The case involved a challenge to the modification of punishment from dismissal to compulsory retirement for a Postal Assistant, M. Duraisamy, who admitted to defrauding Rs. 16,59,065/- via fraudulent withdrawals and non-credit of deposits in RD accounts. The Disciplinary Authority imposed removal from service, which the Central Administrative Tribunal modified to compulsory retirement, citing the respondent's 39 years of unblemished service and restitution of funds. The High Court upheld this. The Supreme Court examined whether the Tribunal and High Court erred in interfering with the quantum of punishment, emphasizing the limited scope of judicial review in departmental disciplinary matters and reliance on precedents affirming non-interference absent procedural defects.
legal_provisions_cited: B.C. Chaturvedi v. Union of India, (1995) 6 SCC 749
Chairman & Managing Director, V.S.P. & Others v. Goparaju Sri Prabhakara Hari Babu, (2008) 5 SCC 569
Maruti Udyog Ltd. v. Ram Lal, (2005) 2 SCC 638
State of Bihar v. Amrendra Kumar Mishra, (2006) 12 SCC 561
Regional Manager, SBI v. Mahatma Mishra, (2006) 13 SCC 727
State of Karnataka v. Ameerbi, (2007) 11 SCC 681
State of M.P. v. Sanjay Kumar Pathak, (2008) 1 SCC 456
Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Surji Devi, (2008) 2 SCC 310
final_judgment: The Supreme Court set aside the orders of the Tribunal and the High Court, restored the punishment of removal from service imposed by the Disciplinary Authority, and held that the interference with the quantum of punishment was unwarranted given the gravity of misconduct and the well-reasoned decision of the Disciplinary Authority.
